input.command: List every HTTP route in nollama.py
input.prompt:
This is a research-only task. Do NOT edit any file.

In the repo at C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\subagent-probe, the main Flask server lives in nollama.py (repo root). Read it and find EVERY HTTP route it exposes.

Be thorough ("very thorough"):
- Search for all Flask route registrations: @app.route(...), @app.get/post/put/delete(...), any add_url_rule(...) calls, and any blueprint registrations.
- Note the HTTP method(s) for each route — the explicit methods= argument, or the default GET (plus HEAD/OPTIONS implied by Flask — report only what's declared, not what Flask implies, but mention if a route declares multiple methods).
- The file may register Ollama-compatible routes on a separate port/surface (e.g. /api/... routes) — include those too. Also check for routes defined anywhere else in the file, e.g. lambdas passed to add_url_rule, or a second Flask app instance.
- Do not confuse helper functions with routes; only actual HTTP endpoints.

Return in your final message a complete list of every route path with its HTTP method(s), one per line, in the form:
METHOD path  (or "GET+POST path" if multiple)
Also note the file:line for each route registration so it can be verified, and mention any route that is registered twice (e.g. on both the OpenAI and Ollama surfaces).

```
POST   /v1/chat/completions       (nollama.py:6228, ollama_app)
```

### Notes on duplicates and structure

- **Paths registered on both surfaces** (deliberate, per the comment at lines 5405–5409 and 6230–6232 — RAG/Copilot clients configured with a single base URL must work whether the Ollama port exists or not):
  - `POST /api/embed` — line 5410 (app) and line 5752 (ollama_app); both delegate to the same `_ollama_embed_body()` helper.
  - `POST /api/embeddings` — line 5416 (app) and line 5758 (ollama_app); both delegate to `_ollama_embeddings_legacy_body()`.
  - `POST /v1/chat/completions` — line 5474 (app) is the real handler; line 6228 (ollama_app) is a thin wrapper that calls `chat_completions()` directly (for Copilot Chat 0.53+, which sends OpenAI chat on the Ollama port).
  - `GET /` appears on both apps but with different behaviour: web UI (app) vs the literal `"Ollama is running"` string (ollama_app).
- **Multi-method routes:** none — every route declares exactly one method (or the default GET for `/` on both apps).
- **No third app, no Blueprints, no `add_url_rule`, no lambda-registered routes.** The only other Flask-app-level hooks are the two `before_request` debug loggers, which are not endpoints.
- Each app is served on its own port via `_serve_app()` (lines 7183 and 7195); the Ollama app is only started when `--ollama-port` is non-zero, which is exactly why the mirrored routes exist on the primary app.

state.title: Find all HTTP routes

part.text:
All 21 routes across the two Flask apps (`app` + `ollama_app`):

**Primary app (OpenAI surface)**
- GET `/`
- GET `/health`
- GET `/v1/models`
- POST `/v1/embeddings`
- POST `/api/embed`
- POST `/api/embeddings`
- POST `/v1/cancel`
- POST `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
- POST `/v1/chat/completions`

**Ollama app (`--ollama-port`)**
- GET `/` (returns "Ollama is running", not the web UI)
- GET `/api/version`
- POST `/api/embed`
- POST `/api/embeddings`
- GET `/api/tags`
- POST `/api/show`
- POST `/api/chat`
- POST `/api/generate`
- POST `/api/pull` (stub)
- DELETE `/api/delete` (stub)
- POST `/api/copy` (stub)
- POST `/v1/chat/completions` (delegates to the primary handler)

`/api/embed`, `/api/embeddings`, and `/v1/chat/completions` are deliberately registered on both surfaces; every route declares exactly one method.
